EcoVessel Summit TriMax Triple Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Flip Straw - 24 Ounces I thought for sure this would be my final bottle. Double stainless steel + a copper lining? Sounds amazing. Tall and thinner than most so it fits in cup holders? Nice! Multiple lid options available for purchase? Cool.

Thing is I tried this next to my other bottles and this was by far the worst at keeping drinks cold. Ice melted in 3 hours or less every time I tried, that’s with half a tray of ice cubs + refrigerated water. All others kept the ice solid for at least 6+ hours.

The style of the bottle is a 5. But if it cannot keep ice from melting and drinks cold as long as my other bottles and tumblers? It’s useless to me. May be good for at home when you can constantly refresh ice and drinks. When traveling? It’s not going to work for me and that’s the main reason I got it. I feel very disappointed especially when they send me emails bragging about how they keep drinks colder way longer than others claim to. They don’t they’re the opposite or what they claim to be.

I tried to review it on their site, but couldn’t get it approved so the product has 5 stars there but I wouldn’t trust that star count.

*update* got a different brand and decided to compare how fast they lose their ability to stay cool. This bottle went from 35 degree water to 66.3 in 3.5 hours. While the other bottle took over 24 hours to get that warm.
text_fidelity_b: EcoVessel Summit TriMax Triple Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Flip Straw - 24 Ounces

text_fidelity_a:
SANYO KATANA SCP 6600 BLUE SPRINT CAMERA CELL PHONE I bought this phone to replace my 2 1/2-year old Samsung Vi660. I've been a big fan of the Samsung line, and thought about buying their comparable version to the Katana (the A900) but the reviews of the Katana's superior battery life won me over. I am not much for the fancy features of cell phones - I just wanted a slimmer phone that had a lower radiation emissions level than the Vi660, a built-in speakerphone, and bluetooth connectivity. After using the phone for a few weeks, here are my impressions so far:

The good:

* Excellent sound quality (in each direction) and none of that "echo" effect I used to get with the Samsung
* Long battery life with many powersaving features
* Beautiful screen, and with web access, is capable of diplaying Google satellite/map info that is just as clear as it is on a PC
* Menu design is very functional, with Favorites and Contacts being directly accessable through the touch of a button
* The "Favorites" button brings up a customizable list of 12 shortcuts, which can be either web addresses or any tool/function/menu item within the phone's own menus (it's like having a programmed navigation button with 12 different options)
* This phone emits the least radiation of any phone in the Sanyo line, and is in the bottom half of the list when compared to other manufacturers (the top being the highest emitters).
* Did you lose your Katana? Send it a specific text message and upon receiving it, the phone will lock itself up, erase its contents, and display a "lost phone" message on the outside screen with the sprint customer service phone number
* The center navigation button links directly to the "Missed Alerts" feature, which keeps a running list of missed voicemails and text messages
* Bluetooth functionality is wonderful. It is easy to make and receive calls from the bluetooth headset, and the sound quality is almost better than that from the in-phone microphone
* The phone has four different types of vibration patterns that you can assign to different types of calls/text messages, and an easily accessable "silence all" feature (no rings, no button beeps, etc) that is ideal for business meetings
* There is a feature on the Katana that allows you to screen calls as the callers are leaving a message
* Menus and Contact information are arranged for easy text-messaging access and message drafting

The bad:

* The VGA camera is not the greatest, and pictures are usually come out with a blueish or orangish cast unless the color balance is adjusted manually beforehand (settings to do this are on the phone)
* Sound quality from the speakerphone is great but the microphone isn't sensitive enough, and my callers frequently complain that I sound too far away
* The only feature I sorely miss from the Samsung phones is their far-superior voice dialing capability, which is second-to-none. The Katana relies on user-recorded tags for its voice recognition capabilities, whereas the Samsung phones just recognized my voice without any prior setup. That functionality also let me dial any phone number by saying the digits; a feature lacking in the Katana. Voice recognition does work, however sometimes you must repeat the name a few times to get it to work. If good voice dialing capabilites are a dealbreaker for you, I'd stick with the Samsung line.
* the charging port on the Katana is on the side of the phone, covered by a rotating rubber insert that is a bit flimsy. This makes it awkward to talk on the phone while it is connected to a charger.
* The volume controls on the side of the phone are on the upper portion of the handset and they are *very* slim, making them a bit hard to use.

The Katana seems to be marketed towards a slightly less business-oriented demographic (it's available in cherry-blossom pink, that should be your first clue), and its features reflect this. This is more of a phone for the casual user who is interested in a stylish phone with good basic functionality, and doesn't need many of the fancier functions of its competitors.

6 MONTH UPDATE: Would I buy it all over again? Maybe, maybe not.
It's been almost 6 months since I bought my Katana, and I have to say, I'm on the fence about it. It isn't a bad phone, it gets STELLAR reception compared to the old Samsung, texting is a snap, and its got a great screen for web browsing. But I've given up a lot of great features on my old Samsung and I don't seem to have gained a whole lot of new ones. I don't ever use the speakerphone because everyone asks if I'm having problems with my connection. I am really missing the ability to digit dial by voice. Talking on the phone with the charger sticking out of the side (especially in the car) is pretty awkward, as is trying to connect the charger when you don't exactly have your hands free. Sprint gives you 2 weeks to make up your mind on the phone, I'd take a look at these issues during that time and try to decide how much of an issue these things really are.
text_fidelity_b: SANYO KATANA SCP 6600 BLUE SPRINT CAMERA CELL PHONE

Ultimate Body Press Wall Mounted Doorway Pull Up Bar Wow, what a monster! This ULTIMATE BODY PRESS WALL-MOUNTED DOORWAY PULL UP BAR is a serious piece of exercise equipment--the bar measures 4 inches around. This allows a solid, comfortable, non-tiring grip for large hands. A heavy duty pull up bar like this one is an excellent choice if you have limited space for exercise equipment--you can use it for resistance band exercises as well as for pull ups.

But the bar does require a fair amount of space (an over door space about 38 inches wide). You mount the bar on the solid "king studs" located about 3 inches on each side of most interior doorways. Thus you will need a doorway that allows you to reach those studs. Some of my condo's doorways are set flush against an interior wall on one side, and are totally unsuitable for mounting this bar.

Also, you need ceilings that are high enough to allow you some headroom for pull ups. My condo has 8 foot ceilings, and most of the doorways leave 15 inches above the opening. This is enough room, but just barely. If you use the bar for resistance band training, you need adequate space to move around in front of the doorway, too.

The installation hardware (lag bolts and washers) is included. However, you will need some tools in order to install the bar--an electronic stud finder, a level, a power drill, a 5/16" drill bit, a socket drive adapter for the power drill (optional but recommended), a 17mm socket wrench, and a 17mm open socket wrench. The sheet of installation instructions (in English) is extremely clear and easy to follow.
text_fidelity_b: Ultimate Body Press Wall Mounted Doorway Pull Up Bar

My Tuomico 20PSI failed the first day of use on the beach in Sullivan's Island SC. In my experience, the first stage blower motor is the most fragile part, and may either last for many uses or fail on the first or second use. This was a hot day at the beach, and my larger size SUP, and the pump started screeching and changing speed noticeably and then died. The SUP was nearly inflated (almost ready for the 2nd stage) and I was quite disappointing. After a few minutes the 2nd stage pump started by itself and finished the inflation to target pressure. However, after the unit fully cooled the first stage never worked again and I returned the pump for a refund. I think the motor burned up. I keep looking for a higher quality pump, and with a large SUP, I may pre-pump a couple minutes to reduce blower time & over-heating. Sleeping Bag, Ohuhu Lightweight Sleeping Bag 3 Season Warm Weather Portable Compact Sleeping Bags for Adult Kids with Carry Bag for Camping Hiking Backpacking and Outdoors 59℉-77℉ For the price, this is a pretty well-made sleeping bag. It's very lightweight, so it's not something you'd want to use in the winter (or even fall) but for more temperate times of the year, it performs well. It's also great for "indoor camping" or sleepovers since it's so lightweight and easy to tote.

The zipper is a critical point and, while this is not a real heavy-duty zipper, it's better than the ones I've seen on other similar sleeping bags. You do need to work the zipper slowly to ensure you don't get the fabric caught in the teeth, but the overall zipper build quality and action is better than I expected. It's a two-way zipper, so you can unzip the base, but keep the side zipped up.

The fabric is poly and is very smooth to the touch. I didn't find any loose threads or puckered seams. The fill is also 100% poly, and is nicely distributed without any lumps or bunches. While the fill is thin, I found it pretty comfortable to sleep in provided that you use a ground pad.

The only negative, and the reason for the loss of one star, is the carry pouch. It's very small. That's good since when you get the sleeping bag into the carry pouch, it takes up surprisingly little room. However, getting the sleeping bag back into the pouch is a real chore. You have to fold the bag up, then roll it very, very tightly to stand even a small chance of getting it to fit into the pouch. The straps on the carry pouch are also rather finicky to adjust. A slightly larger pouch, with better straps, would be a big improvement.

The pouch aside, this is a good lightweight bag that is priced well, but still has decent build quality. Well worth considering.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Sleeping Bag, Ohuhu Lightweight Sleeping Bag 3 Season Warm Weather Portable Compact Sleeping Bags for Adult Kids with Carry Bag for Camping Hiking Backpacking and Outdoors 59℉-77℉

Saver Pad Set I had an accident on my skateboard yesterday, hit my elbow pretty hard and quit for the day. I was going to wait for this protective gear before I started practicing Ollies or doing anything else risky, but my sore elbow was a good reminder to wait for the proper equipment to use before something like that (or worse) happened again.
This set of knee, elbow and wrist protectors is fairly well-made although light. The only thing I really don't like is the logo. After years in graphic-arts I have decided that I truly dislike high-visibility logos so I remove them by sanding or cutting them off. In the case of this "Triple-eight" with a horrible intersection of 3 eights the best method was flat black enamel paint that seems to have obliterated everything except the raised portions of the embroidery. Otherwise it's all black and low key. (This was my intent when I bought this kit and it worked well. Yay!)
The fit is fairly good for a mass-produced set of items, the big factor and the determination for S-M-L being the hand and wrist-guard, which I ordered Large. It's a little loose, but I have all sorts of foam sheets and leather pieces to custom-fit these important pieces, even to reinforcing the external portions as required. The knee and elbow pads are sort of a one-size-fits-all, but the same rules for modification apply.
Essentially, a very good buy for protection that is far better to have and not need than to really need and not have!
This is important stuff to wear, because a skateboard can become very dangerous suddenly without any warning. This kit, in conjunction with a decent helmet and good shoes (skate shoes) can make the difference in protecting those parts of your body that won't function very well unless they move freely without pain. Try being an artist or musician with a broken wrist. Try driving you car or riding your bike with a bad elbow or knee. It's in your best interest to protect yourself, because nobody else will, and if you still haven't figured it out getting hurt costs $$$!
text_fidelity_b: Saver Pad Set

The bag itself is an attractive maroon and large enough to accommodate most adults comfortably. I was most impressed by the zippers which open and close without snagging or catching and can be operated from inside as well as out. The outer shell is water proof and the interior is quite soft and comfortable. It has a loop for hanging and comes with a carrying bag. It is

I do a fair amount of travel for work and often encounter inclement weather and conditions where the roads are temporarily impassable. I have replaced my emergency blanket and pillow with this sleeping bag. folded up it is reasonably compact. I slept in it already a couple of times to test it and was surprisingly comfortable and warm. It appears to be constructed with care and I am impressed with its quality and performance.

text_fidelity_a:
LESOVI Smart Bike Tail Light, Brake Sensing LED Rear Light, Ultra Bright Warning, Auto On/Off Bike Light, IPX6 Waterproof Bicycle Lights, Cycling Safety Back Taillight(6 Light Mode Options) I've got two other lights similar to this one and picked this one up for our five year old's bike. Unlike the other two, this came with both mounting options for the seat post or under the saddle. I initially tried the seat post, but decided that I wanted better visibility.
Swapping mounts was easy enough. I have another light that provides the upper section of the saddle mount, whereas this one relies on zip ties. I would have preferred the upper section.
Nevertheless, it works well enough.

As for the light itself, I chose the auto mode so that our five year old wouldn't have to remember each time they rode. The auto motion mode works as well as expected. It activates when they start to move. It gets brighter when they brake. And it turns itself off when the bike idles.

Overall, I'm happy with this safety addition to the bike. The older the kids get, the more riding we'll do and practicing safety for us is a big deal.

Also, There was no sticker in the box or the packaging.
text_fidelity_b: LESOVI Smart Bike Tail Light, Brake Sensing LED Rear Light, Ultra Bright Warning, Auto On/Off Bike Light, IPX6 Waterproof Bicycle Lights, Cycling Safety Back Taillight(6 Light Mode Options)

text_fidelity_a:
Cygolite Metro 850 Lumen USB Rechargeable Bicycle Headlight, Black I've been using this light now for a couple of days so here are some initial thoughts. The light seems very well made. Solid construction with a solid mounting bracket. The charge port seems very well sealed as well. About my only complaint was that the mounting bracket barely fit on my large frame size handlebars. Although it doesn't get in the way of my shifting or brake cables, I can see a configuration where it would. A more adaptable mounting mechanism may be in order to handle a larger number of bike variants.

My initial response was that I wish it had more light modes but after using it on the streets and trails round Boston I've found 2 that I switch between and I'm happy. The "Steady Pulse" works well for traffic notification. I've watched cars very specifically react to the light at a good distance even though I'm angling it down to not blind too many people. I can also see it flicker on reflective paint on signs so I know it's got good distance. I also use the low setting for dark bike baths so I don't blind oncoming bikers/runners. I can also easily angle it to one side or the other as well to get it out of people's faces.
text_fidelity_b: Cygolite Metro 850 Lumen USB Rechargeable Bicycle Headlight, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Rep Fitness Adjustable Bench – AB-3000 FID – Flat/Incline/Decline I spent a LOT of time researching benches (really, way too much time), but bottom line was that I wanted something stable, adjustable, and of course I didn't want to break the bank. There are a lot of really questionably pricey benches out there -- and when it comes down to it a bench is a very simple piece of equipment. Why are they so expensive? After all of my time investment I am confident in saying that absolutely no other bench on the market combines the features of this bench and its low price.

Specifics:

Delivery -- Typical, left outside of my house.

Packaging -- Decent. The inner boxes were a bit torn up as Rep didn't put enough padding in place. But none of the parts were damaged.

Instructions -- Complete joke. The "assembly" instructions are a single page parts diagram and then a second page of "tips." Come on, at least provide a step-by-step guide? Please visit any IKEA store to learn how it's done.

Assembly -- The instructions are not completely useless; everything can be figured out from the diagram. There is some mention of videos to be watched, but I couldn't be bothered. Overall it wasn't bad but it definitely took longer than the stated 15 minutes -- probably closer to 45.

The biggest issue for me was getting the seat bolted into place. The "tips" sheet shows it being done with the cushion up, which would require some extreme form of dexterity that I don't possess. After a while I realized that I could un-bolt the seat from the base of the unit (this requires removing a bolt that comes already in place from the factory) and then just flip the whole thing back -- after that the rest of the assembly was very simple.

Note that the bolts are a bit on the large side. Neither of my two ratchet sets had anything quite big enough (mine go up to 9/16"), so I had to use a combination of an adjustable wrench and the provided sheet metal "multitool." This undoubtedly slowed me way down.

Overall assembly includes screwing in maybe 8 bolts for the seat and back, two for the ankle pads, and then another four or so for the rest of the unit. Then you go through and tighten everything down, including the bolts that were put on at the factory.

Utilization -- Once assembled, the unit feels extremely sturdy. It sits perfectly on the floor without rocking, and gives me full confidence. The pads are plenty comfortable in my opinion; sure they're a bit stiff, but it's not like I'm going to take a nap on the thing. Also I suspect that these pads will hold up better over time than softer ones would.

Adjustment is simple for both the seat and the back and there are plenty of options for what I need to get done on a daily basis. One important note is that when flat or in decline there is definitely a considerable gap between the seat and back. I know this bothers a lot of people. I don't mind it and don't find it uncomfortable, but I do notice it; if you're looking for something gap-free, look elsewhere.

Not much else to say. I think despite the few flaws, for the price this bench is absolutely unbeatable and will serve me for many years. I'm very happy with my purchase...and I can use the money saved to buy more weights to test that 1,000 pound capacity limit!
text_fidelity_b: Rep Fitness Adjustable Bench – AB-3000 FID – Flat/Incline/Decline

text_fidelity_a: BBAhandware 27.7x18.2x16 in Folding Table Portable Large Camping Table Ultra Light Folding Beach Table Camping with Carrying Bag,Withstands Weights of Up to 55lbs (Silver) I'm not a serious prepper or anything, but I did live 5 days last February without power during the blizzard in Texas.  I have spent the subsequent months getting ready for another time like that again.  The video I watched was a cool way to heat an area in your house when the power is off.  I already had the rectangular paving stones/bricks to place on this table as well as the little alcohol burners.  The idea is to place the cement stones/bricks (the flat ones, not the large ones with holes in them) around the alcohol burner.  The alcohol burner transfers heat to the bricks which in turn release the stored heat over a longer time in the area where they are set up.  Obviously this can't be set up on the floor, so a table that can handle the stored heat is what I needed.  I set the cement blocks up on this metal camping table, put the alcohol burner in the middle and let it "work."  This camping table is the perfect size for my emergency room warming set up with the bricks an burner.  I know it will work fine for a table to use my propane cookstove on as well, but for the moment it is in an emergency box in my house along with the cement bricks and the alcohol burner (and a bottle of rubbing alcohol).  I'm very happy with how this table worked out for my purposes.
text_fidelity_b: BBAhandware 27.7x18.2x16 in Folding Table Portable Large Camping Table Ultra Light Folding Beach Table Camping with Carrying Bag,Withstands Weights of Up to 55lbs (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
SHIMANO UN55 BB Square Taper Bottom Bracket I only have one ride in with this BB so far, but already I can tell it's a night-and-day improvement over the vintage BB it replaces.

I tooled up to overhaul the old BB on a ca. 1990 Trek, and that went well except for the condition of the spindle; it had already become pitted from foreign objects grinding around in there.

The new UN55 is butter smooth and feels more solid, too.

My only reservation is the spacing. I measured slightly under 113mm on the old spindle, so figured the 113mm UN55 would be the tiniest bit wide. In fact it was a tiny bit narrow, as the chainrings lined up slightly to the left of where they were. I adjusted the limit screw and tension on the front derailleur and the bike seems to work fine now. Not sure whether I should try a wider BB or what; I'm new to proper road bike mechanics. Also I didn't actually measure the new spindle to verify that it really is 113mm; I only noticed the discrepancy after I assembled the whole thing and I didn't want to back out all the parts just to measure....

My UN55 was shipped from Bell's Bike Shop and it was missing the bolts. I had to go to a local store and get a couple of spare bolts from their parts bin.
text_fidelity_b: SHIMANO UN55 BB Square Taper Bottom Bracket

text_fidelity_a: Wastou Bike Lights, Super Bright Bike Front Light 1200 Lumen, IPX6 Waterproof 6 Modes Cycling Light Flashlight Torch with USB Rechargeable Tail Light(USB Cable Included) Not nearly as bright as I had hoped. I bought a Radwagon 4 and I wanted to add more light to the underwhelming stock headlight. This light has a couple problems for me. First, it isn't all that bright. It is maybe just a tiny bit brighter than the stock light. Second, the focus of the light, or in other words the size of the bright disc of light it throws, is the same size as the stock Radwagon 4 light. So the effect of the light is very minimal and I think I will end up buying another, bigger, brighter light to do what this one could not. I should have known, to be honest. There is no end to cheap, chinese flashlights and headlights with exaggerated claims about brightness along with long exposure photos taken at night to make them look powerful. I would pass on this one if you honestly need good lighting. This is really better for being seen by cars than for you to see where you are riding.
text_fidelity_b: Wastou Bike Lights, Super Bright Bike Front Light 1200 Lumen, IPX6 Waterproof 6 Modes Cycling Light Flashlight Torch with USB Rechargeable Tail Light(USB Cable Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Brita Plastic Water Filter Bottle, Coral, 26 Ounce, 1 Count I have been using a Brita squeeze bottle for a couple of years and it has been great when on trips. I definitely have saved money by replacing filters instead of plastic water bottles. I was interested in using this hard bottle from Brita, as using a straw-type nozzle is a lot easier than using a bottle you have to squeeze. The bottle is good and it’s designed well, But, there’s one glaring issue with this bottle.

This is a hard bottle that is resistant to drops and scratches, and will bounce when dropped from sufficient height without breaking.

I like the fact that the cap pops up to reveal a silicone straw, and the bottle has an insert in it that allows the drinker to pull up water from the bottom without inverting the bottle. This is a nice change from how the squeeze bottle is used, which must be inverted. Flow is easy too – the water comes out with little effort.

So, Brita left out one very important detail. The filters for these bottles are a charcoal cylinder through which water is forced, and it is normal to get charcoal dust out of the filter when it’s flushed before first use. So, when using the squeeze bottles, Brita says to flush the filter by filling the bottle and forcing the water through, discarding that first bottle full. This bottle cannot be squeezed, and there are no instructions in the package on how to flush the filter for use with it. Following the instructions with the product description, I flushed the filter under running water for 15 seconds. I then put the filter in my squeeze bottle, and when I forced the water through it initially came out purple-ish black as expected. After it was flushed, there was no more charcoal dust and it was ready for this bottle. Is the user expected to flush the filter by spitting out that first bottle full? I hope not, but without instructions saying otherwise there’s little alternative. The charcoal is not dangerous, of course, but it’s very unappetizing.

This is actually a great bottle and Brita did a good job with it. The issue is with the lack of ability to flush the filter to clear out the charcoal dust. There either needs to be a better instruction set to explain, or there needs to be a tool in the box for properly flushing the filter. If Brita can resolve this problem, this would be a very easy recommend; as it stands, I have reservations about that unless there’s a way to flush the filter without relying on another bottle to do it.
text_fidelity_b: Brita Plastic Water Filter Bottle, Coral, 26 Ounce, 1 Count

text_fidelity_a:
Simmons 20-60X60 Venture Black Fmcwptripodhard/Soft Case This old bird still has some of the original low power hunting scopes made by Simmons back in the day. I always wondered why my Dad had a 4X Leupold scope on his .22 while I had a Simmons 4X. Although the Simmons did an acceptable job, it was in no way comparable to the Leupold. Of course my Dad's .22 rimfire rifle was also far superior to the Sears model that he bought for me. But believe me, I was just thrilled at age 10 to be able to go squirrel hunting. And since I trained all winter at the local armory, I could hold my own against him.

But enough of the old days. Simmons then was considered a fairly mediocre manufacturer. Now Simmons is a brand owned by Bushnell Corporation (acquired by them in 2008) which in turn is owned by Vista Outdoor. Competition in the optics market and great strides made in this technology has resulted in current offerings superior in quality and also very reasonably priced. That is an example of "value engineering" at its finest.

This Simmons spotting scope was shipped in a hard case and had the scope itself also wrapped in plastic and inside a separate soft case. Well protected indeed! A bench sized tripod is also included as are directions for both locating the instruction manual and for registering the product for potential warranty coverage. Fear not for the instruction sheet is offered in five languages.

Being an older guy and not a hunter, I don't have to worry about lugging this rather large scope through the bushes. However it does serve two needs for me. The first is that it is extremely useful when testing .22 ammo at a 100 yard range. These old eyes are not what they used to be and this Simmons scope makes it simple to track and score my shots. Most of my shooting is suppressed and testing various subsonic ammo has been interesting to say the least.

Since we live on beautiful Charlotte Harbor in Southwest Florida, Mother Nature offers us constant reminders of how the animal kingdom functions and survives. Being able to focus on long distances off our back lanai has really increased our visual reach even to the far shore. We are able to watch Bald Eagles and Osprey fish, Red Tailed Hawks and Florida Barred Owls home in on their prey, and alligators and manatees cruise through the harbor. Entertaining for us and our guests.

For roughly $150.00 this is a heck of a deal for the quality you receive. Simmons has worked its way back into being competitive with most of the mainstream firms. If you're looking for a big increase in quality, plan on spending a lot more money. In the old days we would call this "the law of diminishing returns". That means that you have to spend a lot more money just to get an incremental return in actual performance. Simmons proves that you don't have to spend that much.
text_fidelity_b: Simmons 20-60X60 Venture Black Fmcwptripodhard/Soft Case

Texan Classics Utility Hybrid Iron-Wood #2 Golf Club OK - my own fault as by now, I know you get what you pay for. On this basis, buying a $20 hybrid is more experiment than sensible purchase. But based on prior reviews, I thought, why not?

Here's why not: I received the club on Wednesday, put it in my bag and went to the course on Thursday. Looks like a Taylormade Rescue, but with really poor detail. Well, looks don't get the ball down the course, and it was $20, so who cares, right?

First shot, nicely impressed...second shot, the same. Third shot, I feel something...odd. Ball pops straight up in the air at almost a 90 degree angle to my lie. Look at the club, and there's the answer. Clubhead is an inch down the shaft from the ferrule, and with the slightest tug, it pops right off. So much for the experiment.

Maybe I'm crazy, but there's just no excuse for a clubhead falling off within three shots; six swings total with practice. None. Zero. I'm surprised it actually made it through shipping without coming off. Maybe they used cornstarch to glue this on instead of epoxy? Who knows. text_fidelity_a:
OutSmart Gear 3 in 1 Ultralight Titanium Spork | Portable and Reusable Multi Tool for Backpacking and Camping | Feed Your Face, Leave No Trace I really wanted to love this. I still love the idea, but the execution isn't quite there. The light weight is amazing. Titanium is legit. The combination of a spoon on one end and a fork sounds like a winner, as you forego the compromises of a spork. Sadly for some reason neither the fork nor the spoon are great. The fork is oddly wide, which we'll get to later. Likewise the spoon isn't too deep. Neither the fork nor the spoon are ideal.

I might have still someone gave this 5 stars (titanium is that cool!), but alas there's the serrated edge. It's not really useful, and when combined with the wide fork, it means you'll be tearing at you gums unless you have a huge mouth. That's kinda a dealbreaker. I could see past the other issues in a camping/backpacking context, but tearing your gums just isn't fun!

Still gave it 4 stars if you have a big (or at least wide) mouth.
text_fidelity_b: OutSmart Gear 3 in 1 Ultralight Titanium Spork | Portable and Reusable Multi Tool for Backpacking and Camping | Feed Your Face, Leave No Trace

SYLVANIA RX2 OSRAM LED Bicycle Taillight This is a 2.4 lux/4 lumen rain proof and splash proof bicycle taillight which takes 2 AAA batteries (not included). These batteries should provide 36 hours of illumination according to the package.

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this light. First, it's practically impossible to remove the cover to insert the batteries. There's a notch at the bottom of the light that is used to open the compartment. I had to use a letter opener to pry it open while squeezing the top a bit. The force that had to be used damaged the plastic around the notch but did not affect the light's functionality. There are four plastic prongs that hold the top reflector onto the base and I can see these prongs breaking when opening or closing the compartment to replace the batteries.

I have a Trek bike and it was difficult to position on my bike because the height of the light got in the way of the reflector that was already there. However, the mounting bracket is a typical bracket that clenches itself around the bike frame. The light clips onto the fastener and can be removed and used elsewhere, such as clipping onto a backpack or hat for use when walking.

The light turns on via a button on the back. Only the top "bulging" part lights up as the bottom acts as a reflector.

Because of the difficulty of opening this light and chance for breakage during battery replacement, I personally cannot recommend this. This is not a light I would purchase after having tried it.

There are bag coolers that have thicker walls than this, but this should be fine when transporting groceries home in the summer. I would not fill the entire product with cans and ice, like the marketing photo shows, since this would likely stress the seams too much. Use a solid plastic cooler for heavy items like that.

I would prefer if coolers had a plastic shelf on the bottom to keep the items away from melted water or spilled liquids that collect on the bottom. Most coolers do not have this feature. I have been using plastic liners that I took from my Tupperware produce storage containers.

The current price is $39. I see less expensive coolers that are probably just as good.

Features that some other coolers have are wheels for transporting heavy items, and some can be plugged into a car outlet or wall outlet for refrigeration. Other coolers collapse more when put into storage. This one is not designed to be collapsed, although it can be smooshed into a smaller shape when not in use. Good coolers can last many years, so you might want to invest in a high-quality one.

text_fidelity_a:
Housmile Exercise Stability Yoga Ball, Perfect Ball Chair for Home or Office (Purple 55cm) i received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased review. I was not influenced by anyone in any way.

Yoga balls are a great exercise item. I have a hard time doing sit ups and using the Yoga Ball, helps with doing them much easier. I used to be able to do pushups, putting my feet on the yoga ball and hands on the floor and do my pushups, but well yeah, that was a while back. So can not do that now. These really help with exercising the abs, waist, back, arms, hips, leg, gluts and other muscles. They are great for sitting at your desk. It forces proper spine alignment. Another great thing about using this alternative to a chair, is that you can do stretches or mini-workouts whenever you want, without getting up.

Your body primarily uses your core (abdominal) muscles to help compensate for changes in balance. So, you are essentially getting a low-key abdominal workout. Doesn't sound like much huh? But just consider the amount of time you spend on your computer at the office, or at home. Those hours can build up, and result in a strengthening of ab muscles. Not having a chair back to slouch into or armrests to lean on, you're almost forced to keep your back straight, which can encourage better posture. So get on that Yoga Ball and get movin! I know I am.

Besides developing good overall muscle tone for your entire body, the yoga ball provides many other benefits like rehabilitating back, hip, and knee injuries and getting a great workout to improve core stability, posture, and muscle balance. By using a low-impact workout, you will also improve your flexibility and your cardiovascular system.
PROS:
helps improve your balance - as we get older especially, we lose balance and mobility.
improves your circulation
you will feel more energetic
it's made with environmental friendly, non-toxic material.

CONS:
not really anything bad to say about a yoga ball. It's "all" good

OVERALL: This Yoga Ball is a quality product. Keeps the air really good.
text_fidelity_b: Housmile Exercise Stability Yoga Ball, Perfect Ball Chair for Home or Office (Purple 55cm)

Most folks have some level of Frisbee skills, and most folks have played a game with a goal/goalie. This piggy-backs off of that common knowledge.

While the game is fun, the parts in this kit are basic. This helps keep the cost down and keeps it highly portable. Both are sound choices, but it would feel better if the actual cost were a bit lower. I'm thinking $25-30 more than close to $40. I'd definitely recommend checking out Kan Jam and related Frisbee games. They're fun! As far as the hardware, this is definitely something I can recommend, but I cannot see why this would be better than another competing product.

text_fidelity_a:
Tepui Camp Lounge Furniture Lawn chairs are useful for many purposes. They come in handy when you attend events and are a practical addition to your backyard. They are not all created equally, though, and one of the better ones I have used is this chair, the Tepui Single Chair.

Taken from its transporting bag, this lawn chair is ready to use- you just have to pull the legs apart and stand it up. It has a cup holder for drinks and I like that it is placed below the chair, attached to the leg. With other lawn chairs, the cup holder is right there, on the arm of the chair, and your drink can get in the way of resting your arm. I also like that the covers on each arm are removable. They are held in place with Velcro and if you don’t prefer them, that is perfectly fine, as they are easy to remove.

With comfort, this chair is better than most. I don’t get that ‘sinking feeling’ like I often do with other lawn chairs. This one feels more secure and the weight limit rating confirms that it is, indeed, stronger than the average lawn chair. Another cool feature is the mesh back. It allows air to flow through and it does make a difference at keeping you cool and preventing perspiration from forming on your back.

This lawn chair is easy enough to fold back up and place into the carrying bag when you’re finished. I should point out that this chair is heavier than others so carrying it for a long distance could be tiring. However, it is also stronger and more durable than others. I am willing to put up with the added weight to have a better lawn chair.

I have several different lawn chairs for home and event use. This lawn chair from Tepui is an excellent one overall, delivering on comfort, quality, and strength. It is the best lawn chair I currently own and now that I have used it a few times, I am ready to toss my other, cheaper chairs in the trash and replace them all with this one. It really is that good!
text_fidelity_b: Tepui Camp Lounge Furniture

MasterPieces NFL Unisex-Adult 100-Piece Casino Style Poker Chips While I was born in the DFW Metroplex, I grew up in Las Vegas. And, honestly, one would think we all have an obligatory set of poker chips at home. I didn’t.

But, I now do. I also have the Golden Knights chips in addition to these ones. So know, both of my “hometowns” are being repped as some would say.

While the team might be questionable quality, these chips are not. They are definitely casino quality and have some weight to them. The entire package (with chips and tray) is enough to be a serious weapon if thrown at someone. You’re going to inflict a moderate if not serious injury. Then again, if someone is breaking into your house …

Anyway …

These do not have a dollar ($) value to them. You can assign your own and they can be used for ANY poker game, blackjack, or any game you want to play. For example (our house, and yes, we’re “cheap” here):

Red – $1
Blue – $5
White – $10
Green – $25
Black – $50

When used, these “sound” just like the casino chips too. In fact, since I haven’t handled real casino chips in a while, these might be better. They are colorful too. The logos are the same on all chips – fronts or backs depending on how you want to view them.

The tray is great quality too. The only problem, and it could be small or huge depending … after use storage.

If you put them back in the box – some chips will fall through the opening. I learned this first hand for a “picture” (hence why these are laying down and NOT standing up). I did manage to tape the inside and outside of the box. It looks tacky, but it keeps the chips in.

As of this review, the chips are $24.99 before tax. And, these are definitely worth it. Great for when you want to play for stakes. Fake is highly recommended due to legal issues.
text_fidelity_b: MasterPieces NFL Unisex-Adult 100-Piece Casino Style Poker Chips

text_fidelity_a: Brunton 7DNL Baseplate Map Compass I've trekked many miles, guided by the same Brunton 7DNL baseplate compass I received from my wilderness survival camp counselor, decades ago.  There are a few scuffs, and the edges aren't pristine, and yet it still works fine.  It's just as accurate as several $20 ~ $80 compasses my peers carry, and has survived a fair amount of abuse.  While it's not as rugged as some other models, for the price you can buy 2 or 3 of them so you have spares.  As well, you won't feel as guilty should one disappear, or be damaged.  Its compact size makes it handy, but also makes it a little harder to get precise bearings.  It also doesn't have true declination adjustment, only an etched-in scale, which can lead to some issues if you forget this nuance.  For casual trips, I'm quite comfortable with relying on the Brunton 7DNL.  For anything more critical, it's my backup compass (to a more-expensive [[ASIN:B000FEWA6S Suunto M-3DL Compass]], which I tend to baby).
text_fidelity_b: Brunton 7DNL Baseplate Map Compass

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Rodvault Fly Fishing Rod Carrier This thing is totally awesome. I was actually unaware that such fishing rod carriers existed. And of course, I barely had to browse other models to tell Thule would be a top contender.

Construction is fantastic. Rigid metal tubes and hardened plastic casing make "vault" an acceptable term for this.

One thing I didn't realize was that with this one (unlike the tackle fishing carriers), the length is not adjustable. The tubing is the same diameter for the entire length, so the two 5' sections connect in the middle with a compression connector tightened by hex screws. Because of this, you probably need to lock both parts of this to your rooftop rack, which leads to me locking...

...Locking this up is probably the weak point for me. This is unfortunate, because I always want better locking on any device, but this one isn't even as good as I might expect out of Thule. For one thing, it doesn't have the "one key" feature that Thule started using at some point (but you had to special order your device with your key type already if you wanted to go with that, so maybe consumers were too lazy to do it and the company gave up on it...not sure). Worse, though - and a real concern - is that this and my tackle vault use the same key, which leads me to wonder if I am able to open up and steal from any Thule rodvault I see out there in the wild? (Of course, I'd like to believe that anyone with enough money to buy a rodvault would be unlikely to steal fishing stuff from another person, but who knows...). Also, you need padlocks to lock the vault to the rack, which isn't that big of a deal, but I've seen other equipment with integrated locks that used the same key as the rest of the equipment, so it could be better.

This is big and heavy. More so than I expected. That adds some sense of value to it, but it also has me rethinking my storage place, especially considering its 10' permanent length unless I want to disassemble it with every use.

I'm also curious if this would hold some deep sea poles. I think so, but don't have any yet to try for myself.

In conclusion, it's hard to not be impressed with this thing, and yet I see some areas for improvement, mostly in the locking scheme. It is hard not to give this a full five stars simply because of its excellent sturdiness and bringing a whole new excellent way to transport large, expensive poles with even a small car, and without having to worry about them at all, for the most part.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Rodvault Fly Fishing Rod Carrier

text_fidelity_a:
OUTAD Outdoor Mummy 40-50 Degree Portable Sleeping Bag for Camping/Hiking/Backpacking I received this as a free review sample. I was surprised by light weight and appreciate how compactly it folds and stores. Since the product description and photos provide all of the physical specs I'll spare you a recitation and will stick to personal observations.

This bag is a lot roomier than I thought, and captures your body heat nicely. Where I am this time of year it rarely dips into the 40s, so I tested it at 55 degrees. It was plenty warm at that temperature, and it also breathed. Ironically, the less you are wearing (at 55 degrees) the warmer you feel after it has had a chance to capture and trap your own body heat.

If you do intend to use it outdoors I recommend a waterproof ground cover or - better - an air mattress. The latter is best on open ground because this bag is thin and you will feel pebbles and even minor differences in ground level. Indoors it's totally comfortable and is perfect for guests. I personally intend to use it throughout the winter because we do get sub freezing temperatures a few times a year in Central Florida, and I prefer to conserve electricity during the cold months.

You have a lot of 'wiggle' room in this bag, and as long as you note the limitations this is a bargain compared to some high end bags that I also own. No, this is not in the same league as those, but for the price this is still a good deal.

Other factors are: it's sturdy and nicely constructed, light weight and less bulky than high end bags, and warm in temperate areas. The specs claim it will work as low as 14 degrees, but I think the recommended 40-50 is closer to the mark.
text_fidelity_b: OUTAD Outdoor Mummy 40-50 Degree Portable Sleeping Bag for Camping/Hiking/Backpacking

text_fidelity_a:
Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow Good anti stress eye pillow. What I like about the Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy pillow
1) I like the fragrance of the lavender and chamomile pillow.
2) The fragrance is not overwhelming it is subtle.
3) It is not overstuffed so it drapes nicely over your eye and sinus area when you are lying flat.
4) The silk has a cooling effect
5) I have chronic sinusitis and this pillow feels like it helps to relieve some of that tight pressure pain. It also seems to calm the area around my eyes.
I have used several different sinus pillow type remedies over the years for that "ahhh relief!" moment when you can feel the swelling and ache diminishing.Not many were very effective but this one and the Lavender eye pillow by AyaZen are both effective. However, I would choose the one from AyaZen over this one because:
1) It can be heated and froze as long as you put it in a plastic sealed bag so it doesn't absorb freezer odor.
2) It has more filling and a more balanced filling making it a little weightier than the Earth Therapeutics eye pillow
3) The velvet like cover of the AyaZen is soft and luxurious yet it also has a griping effect so it doesn't readily slip off your face.
4) It has a stronger lavender scent that is soothing but not overwhelming.
5) For me, this pillow relieves the pain and pressure associated with my sinusitis better.

As a comparison, they are both good eye pillows but AyaZen wins for me.

The reason Earth Therapeutics is not a perfect five stars and doesn't win for me:
1) It doesn't have the balanced filling the AyaZen does
2) The silk used to encase the Earth Therapeutics pillow slips very easily unless you are lying down flat.If your head happens to turn a little while sleeping at an angle or with your head raised at any height, it slips off. Even though you can conform it to your eyes and nose it won't stay because of the silkiness of the material and the almost whisper light weight of the pillow. If your head is raised at any angle or your head happens to fall sideways while napping, you must continually reposition the pillow.
3) you cannot heat it in the microwave or put it in the freezer. I know this pillow is suppose to be Therapeutic based solely on the oils it harbors and the silk that encases it but it just needs a little more to really reach that Therapeutic level.

I bought this based on it conforming to the face and being Therapeutic. However, I often sleep with my head raised up or in my recliner because of breathing issues due to my sinuses.The silk of this pillow would always cause it to slip down or sideways causing me to wake up and recenter it on my eyes. Overall, I would recommend this pillow for someone who doesn't have to sleep with the head or upper body raised at any height and doesn't have to turn their head much while napping. The silk does have a cooling effect and the lavender and chamomile does help to relieve some of the pressure and pain.
text_fidelity_b: Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow

text_fidelity_a:
Extreme Max 3005.2175 Post Trailer Guide-On - 45", Zinc-Plated Uprights with Zinc-Plated Hardware I did a lot of research and landed on this item. I first purchased the 45" version but realized those did not work on my trailer so I replaced with the 65" which is perfect. I have a 19.5' I/O runabout boat with tandem wheel aluminum trailer. I mainly bought so I could see the trailer without the boat when backing, but also use this for loading in wind and/or in deeper water where you can't see the back of the trailer.

This product is strong, reinforced at the corners, metal tubing running up nearly all the way into the PVC, heavy duty PVC and mounting brackets. Those fit a variety of sizes of trailers.

It is not galvanized however, but zinc plated. It will not last in salt water so opt for something different if planning to be in salt or brackish water.

I gave mine a quick waxing before installation (all metal parts) just to add another layer of protection.

Installation was simple. I installed mine under the trailer frame instead of on top. I did have to buy the optional longer bolts based on the instructions, however, the bolts that came with the basic package would have fit. But overall everything was easy, simple and quick to install.

Very professional looking and I would highly recommend, especially over those that only use a small amount of metal going up into the PVC. These can take a good amount of force from your boat.
text_fidelity_b: Extreme Max 3005.2175 Post Trailer Guide-On - 45", Zinc-Plated Uprights with Zinc-Plated Hardware

text_fidelity_a:
bago Lightweight Small Hiking Backpack for Women and Men - 25L Travel Day Pack - Foldable Hiking Daypack Ultralight My husband was looking for a day pack. I bought him 6 backpacks to compare. The [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]], the [[ASIN:B00DNTR5CQ Osprey Packs Momentum 22 Daypack (Spring 2016 Model), Carbide Grey]], the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]], the [[ASIN:B00FUWSTI8 Lightweight Rucksack 25L for men women kids - Foldable into Inner pocket (BLACK)]], the [[ASIN:B013K7CJD0 Cycling Hiking Backpack Sunhiker Water Resistant Travel Backpack Lightweight SMALL Daypack M0714 (Dark Green)]], and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. There were pros and cons for each pack. He decided to keep the [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]]because it met his needs the best. We ordered all packs in gray, green, or black. We returned the other 5 packs. I liked 2 of the lightweight foldable packs - the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]]and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. I decided to order those for myself in Pink and Purple.
All of the packs had a mesh pocket on each side of the pack for water bottles. We tested them all with a Nalgene bottle and a bottle of water. All of the packs could easily hold the bottle of water. Some were a very tight fit for the Nalgene bottles. All packs had a main compartment with one or two pockets in the front of the pack. The main compartments varied from 561 cubic inches to 1386 cubic inches. 3 of the packs were lightweight, foldable, and storable in their own pocket.
Here are my summaries of this pack:
1071 cubic inches
17” x 10.5” x 6”
6 1/2” mesh pockets
Covers about 5 1/2” of bottles
Straps 3” wide
Hard to adjust shoulder straps, especially to loosen them
Straps feel soft and pliable
This pack has 3 main compartments. In the back is the largest zippered compartment. In the middle is a small zippered pocket. In the front is a mesh compartment which is held closed by a strap and buckle. I did not like having a mesh compartment.
Pros:
- Lightweight
- Handle at top of pack for an additional way of carrying it
- Side pockets fit a Nalgene bottle
- Medium sized zippered pouch inside the large compartment – this is where the pack is stored when folded
- Large pocket inside on the back of the large compartment
- 1 extra loop on outside bottom of pack.
- Extra side support straps
Cons:
- No back padding and did not keep it’s shape. Typical for a foldable pack.
- Some padding on the back panel
- Shoulder straps were several layers of mesh but NOT fortified with the nylon fabric
- Things stored in front mesh compartment would get dirtier and wetter than in a pack with a zippered fabric covered compartment.

I returned this pack. It was a nice foldable pack, but I didn't like the mesh pocket in the front.
text_fidelity_b: bago Lightweight Small Hiking Backpack for Women and Men - 25L Travel Day Pack - Foldable Hiking Daypack Ultralight

text_fidelity_a:
Myklops Rear View Mirror On the whole, I'm happy with my purchase and find it very useful when I'm riding. I've got a folding bike, which I love but limits my choice of mirrors. I tried different ones that attach to glasses or helmets, but I could never find one that quite fit; besides, I always worried they would drop off the moment I hit a bump. I figured the Myklops was my best option.

As others have noted, objects in this review are a heck of a lot closer than they appear. However, I've gotten used to this and find the mirror very helpful for spotting cars, trucks, and other larger vehicles in traffic. For spotting other bikes, skateboarders, and standing scooter riders (scooterists?), it's not as helpful. Being smaller, they're usually on me well before I pick them up in the mirror. Luckily, that's usually not a problem. With motorcycles and mopeds/scooters, it's a mixed bag. The bigger they are, they easier they are to pick out in the mirror. Usually it's the noise of their engines that I notice first, then I know to look for them in the mirror. So this mirror is helpful, but not as much as I'd like.

Sturdiness is hard to speak to without lots of time going by, but I've been using this regularly for over six weeks, tossing it into bags when I'm not riding with it, and it's holding up. I find the cover a little fiddly to close, but it does latch into place with a little patience. The biggest challenge was remembering to push the arms back into the base before taking by backpack off once I'd gotten to where I was going, but that's pilot error on my part. I don't yank at the arms or twist them hard, but neither am I super delicate with them. They feel the same as they did out of the package, so I'm hopeful that they'll last a while.

As for stability, I find the mirror to be very stable once I've extended the arms and positioned it how I like. The band sometimes shifts around my wrist as I ride, but I don't think this is a fault of the product. I usually wear long-sleeved shirts, the material of which is often a bit loose, so I need to be more careful about smoothing that down and not letting it bunch before fastening the strap. When I'm wearing shorter sleeves with tighter fitting sun gloves, the band stays in place. Also, I'm very pleased that the velcro on the band is on the gentle side. By that I mean that it doesn't have large teeth of the sort that often damage my clothes. Despite being careful, I sometimes catch my clothing on it, but so far (touch wood) it hasn't caused any pilling or tearing of the fabric ... and these are fairly delicate materials I'm talking about, so that's a major bonus.

I think it's impossible to make a perfect mirror that fits all my riding needs. But this comes pretty darn close. Funnily enough, as I sat down to write this review, I noticed that there's currently a nice little discount for it, no doubt for Black Friday/Cyber Monday/or other seasonal sales holiday here. I paid full price for mine, but I'm okay with that. At full price, I feel like I got my money's worth, and I would definitely buy this again.
text_fidelity_b: Myklops Rear View Mirror
